title: Halal by default
hook: If it feels like everything is haram, here's the truth: most things are allowed.

screens.text: Some days it feels like every post, every person, has a new thing you're "not allowed" to do. Today, a reset: the list of what's allowed is huge, and the list of what's forbidden is short.

**Allowed is the starting point.** *"It is He who created for you all of that which is on the earth"* [Q 2:29, Saheeh Intl.]. Scholars take a principle from verses like this one: in everyday things, the default is **halal** (allowed).
bubbles: Everyday things means food, clothes, hobbies, work and fun.
Something is **haram** (forbidden) only when there's clear evidence for it [Being Muslim, glossary: mubah].

screens.text: **The forbidden list is short,** and you already know most of it: pork, alcohol and drugs, sex outside marriage, interest, gambling, stealing, lying, and harming people.
bubbles: The Prophet ﷺ came to make good things lawful, forbid harmful ones, and lift people's heavy burdens [Q 7:157].
And Allah warns against forbidding the good things He allowed [Q 5:87].

screens.prompt: Halal by default, or one of the few limits?

items.why: Sports, exercise and fun with friends are allowed.
Alcohol is one of the few clear limits. A soda works just as well socially.
Normal clothes are fine, as long as they cover what needs covering.
Your name stays unless its meaning is bad (Day 9).
Gambling is on the short forbidden list.
Most food without pork, alcohol or meat questions is simply allowed.

screens.text: **Gray areas exist, and that's okay.** The Prophet ﷺ said the halal is clear and the haram is clear, and between them are unclear things many people don't know. Whoever steers clear of those protects their faith [Bukhari 52].
bubbles: So in a gray area, ask before you worry. Don't let it make everything feel forbidden.

screens.situation: Chris watches a video where a guy says real Muslims must drop their Western clothes, birthday cakes, non-Muslim friends and their old names. Chris feels like he's failing at everything.

options.text: Remember that halal is the default, and ask his mentor which of these, if any, actually matter
options.feedback: Yes. Most of that list is culture or opinion. A trusted teacher can sort the real limits from the noise.

options.text: Drop all of it tonight to be safe
options.feedback: Not quite. Forbidding what Allah allowed is its own mistake [Q 5:87]. And burnout follows.

options.text: Decide Islam is too strict for him
options.feedback: Not quite. That video isn't Islam's list. The real limits are few, and most of life stays the same.

screens.text: **Why the limits are there.** Each one protects something: your mind (no intoxicants), your body, your family, other people's rights, your money.
bubbles: And Allah teaches gently. The first parts of the Qur'an to come down were about faith and the afterlife. Rules came later, once hearts were settled [Bukhari 4993].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Allah created what is on earth for people [Q 2:29]; eat what is lawful and good [Q 2:168]; don't forbid the good things Allah made lawful [Q 5:87]; the Prophet ﷺ makes lawful the good, forbids the harmful, and lifts burdens [Q 7:157].
- The legal principle that, in worldly matters (food, dress, customs, transactions), the default is permissibility unless evidence forbids it [Being Muslim, glossary: mubah; Research Notes - Core Essentials and Madhab Map (culture vs religion)]. Acts of worship are the opposite: they follow what's taught.
- Clear halal, clear haram, and doubtful things between; avoiding the doubtful protects faith [Bukhari 52].
- Rules came gradually, after faith settled [Bukhari 4993].
- Convert context: information overload and "haram police" online cause burnout and doubt [Research Notes - Retention and Convert Voices, themes 3–4].

**Likely questions**
- *"Is X halal?"* For everyday things with no clear text, start from "allowed," then check: does it involve one of the clear limits (pork, alcohol, intoxicants, interest, gambling, immodesty, harm, deception)? If unsure or contested, say so and offer the imam.
- *"How do I tell culture from religion?"* Ask: is there a verse or authentic hadith behind it, or is it a custom? Point back to Day 9.
- *"My hobby/music/birthday was called haram."* Hobbies: usually fine. Music (Q22) and holidays (Q5) are contested: give the "scholars differ; ask your imam" line and escalate. Birthdays: scholars differ; route to the imam.

**Escalate:** music and entertainment (Q22); holidays (Q5); meat (Q6); finance and interest (Q24); anything the convert wants a personal ruling on.

**Don't**
- Don't declare contested things haram or halal; name the difference and offer the imam.
- Don't add to the forbidden list or play "haram police."
- Don't treat the default-permissibility principle as applying to new acts of worship.

- [Bukhari 52](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:52): the halal is clear, the haram is clear, and doubtful matters between.
- [Bukhari 4993](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4993): Aisha on the order of revelation.
